title: LaMelo Ball's partner Ana Montana was arrested in Mecklenburg County. Then her attorney said a doctor's actions are behind the charges - NewsBreak
text:
By Sayed ,
7 hours ago IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Booking records obtained by TMZ say Ana Montana, identified in those records by her legal name, Analicia Chaves, was taken into custody Monday in Mecklenburg County. The arrest landed months after reports that she and LaMelo Ball had confirmed they were first-time parents earlier this year.
TMZ’s account of the booking records says she faces two felony counts of obtaining a controlled substance by fraud or forgery. The records also list two misdemeanor counts of simple possession of a Schedule IV controlled substance.
According to the paperwork described by TMZ, she was held on a $20,000 bond tied to the felony counts. That paperwork places the alleged conduct on February 21 and lists the warrant as issued on September 22, six days before the Monday arrest.
Her attorney said the allegations stem from a doctor’s actions Chaves’ attorney said the case turns on what a doctor did, not on a plan he said she ran on her own. He argued that she was not involved in any independent scheme.
“To clarify, the charges allege that a doctor who used a fraudulent DEA registration and NPI number prescribed Alprazolam for Ms. Chaves, and that she used the prescription written by the doctor to obtain the prescribed Alprazolam at a pharmacy,” the lawyer said.
“The drug possession charges appear to allege that she possessed the aforementioned Alprazolam upon obtaining it from the pharmacy via the prescription written by the doctor,” the lawyer continued.
In that statement, the lawyer said the charges describe a doctor who used a fraudulent DEA registration and NPI number to prescribe Alprazolam for her. He said she then filled that prescription at a pharmacy, and that the possession counts appear to cover the same Alprazolam after she picked it up.
Public biographical details in the report list her birth date as Oct. 9, 1989, in New Bedford, Massachusetts. Ball was born in 2001, which would put her 12 years older than him. The report says the two were first linked in 2021 and kept much of the relationship out of public view.
Ball posted photos in January 2022 promoting his LaFrance fashion line, and one frame showed a woman who appeared to be Montana stepping into an elevator. That image fed dating speculation at the time. The report says the couple made the relationship Instagram official in 2023.
Away from Ball, she has worked as a model and influencer, with appearances in Smooth and Vibe, according to the report. She has also been featured in music videos for T.I., Rick Ross, and Flo Rida.
The report also traces earlier public links. It says she was linked to Belgian soccer player Axel Witsel in 2013, and that rumors in about 2015 tied her to French soccer star Karim Benzema.
In March 2026, a clip she shared drew fresh attention to her personal life. Montana sighed as Paramore’s Ain’t It Fun played, and text over the video read, “POV: You realize everything you’ve been using your whole life is toxic. And now you have to relearn how to exist.”
The report said some viewers treated the clip as a possible sign of a breakup or strain with Ball. It also said nothing in the post directly suggested she was talking about the then-Hornets star.
The same report describes separate court matters involving Ball, not her drug case. In October 2023, a 12-year-old fan and his family filed a $3.75 million lawsuit accusing Ball of driving away from Spectrum Center and running over the boy’s foot. Ball’s troubles go beyond the lawsuit, as his brother Lonzo has said Lamelo now has a driver because he has a lot of situations on the road. Ball denied the allegations, and the case was settled confidentially in June 2026, the report said.
Agape Property Management Group sued Ball and his manager over two Uptown Charlotte condos, alleging more than $181,500 in unpaid rent and over $90,000 in HOA fines, according to the report. Ball’s financial disputes have drawn legal attention before, as weeks after his Minnesota trade, he was sued over more than $181,000 in unpaid rent. The report said Montana’s charges stand apart from those disputes.
